accessibility: The card title is the level-1 heading; the token field has a visible label, help text tied to it, and an error announced with role="alert" when invalid.
The primary button is the only Iris element and is full width with a 44px target on touch tiers; the token input uses 16px text on phones.
The CLI command wraps rather than overflowing the 384px card on narrow screens.
No text renders below 12px in any Locale; controls use 13px and prose 14px, and zh-TW line heights grow by about 2px.
Light and dark themes meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for text and controls.
constraints: Tokens are never echoed back, logged or stored in the Workspace; the page is part of the host-local access roster flow.
Workbench chrome (Rail, TabBar, top bar) is not shown before sign-in.

Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md: graphite chrome, Iris violet only for selection, focus and the single primary action per region, Marker magenta only for human annotation, and status hues only in badges, icons and alerts.

Every visible string is bound with $i18n. en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets; zh-TW uses Taiwan Traditional Chinese with full-width punctuation and keeps domain nouns (View, Variant, Widget, Workspace, Review, Spec, UX Flow, Handoff, Adapter, Locale, Asset, Decision, Owner, Checks, Evidence) in English.
Identities and measurements stay literal and use the mono blueprint register: Widget ids such as #checkout-submit, Widget type names, revisions, keyboard keys and CLI commands are never translated.
entryConditions: An unauthenticated browser requested any Workbench page, or a session expired.
A sign-in link (#uiux_i_…) in the URL fragment is redeemed automatically and never shown; this page is the fallback when there is no link.

The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset (desktop 1920 × 1080, tablet 1024 × 768, or mobile 390 × 844), one Locale (en-US default or zh-TW), and one theme (light or dark). All twelve combinations are authored and captured explicitly.
spec.intent: Let a person reach a Workspace with as little ceremony as the access model allows: open the single-use sign-in link, or paste a member token, and land where they were going.
interactionRules: The card explains both ways in: open the link that uiux dev or the Owner gave you, or paste a member token.
Sign in validates the pasted token with the server; while it runs the button is disabled and "Signing you in…" is announced (signing-in Variant).
An invalid, expired or already-used credential keeps the pasted value, marks the field invalid and explains that sign-in links work once and expire after 24 hours (invalid-token Variant).
The "No link?" footer shows the literal uiux invite create command that mints a fresh single-use link on the host.
After success the Workbench returns to the page that required sign-in; agents never use this page and authenticate with Authorization: Bearer tokens instead.
